newsitem.title: USA: Attorney pleads guilty in Espy-related trial.
newsitem.headline: Attorney pleads guilty in Espy-related trial.

text.p: A prominent New Orleans attorney pleaded guilty on Monday to making false statements to help the brother of former Clinton Cabinet member Mike Espy get a campaign loan.
Independent Counsel Donald Smaltz, who is investigating Espy for allegedly accepting illegal gifts and favors while he was agriculture secretary, announced the plea in a statement released here.

Smaltz said lawyer Alvarez Ferrouillet pleaded guilty of conspiracy and making false statements to help Henry Espy get a $75,000 campaign loan from the First National Bank of Clarksdale in Mississippi.
The loan was to pay debts resulting from Henry Espy's unsuccessful campaign to obtain the congressional seat vacated by his brother when Mike Espy became agriculture secretary.

Municipal Healthcare Cooperative Inc., which is 50 percent owned by Ferrouillet, also pleaded guilty to making false statements to the bank. The law firm of Ferrouillet & Ferrouillet, which guaranteed the loan, pleaded guilty to conspiracy to defraud the bank.
The pleas came on the opening day of the trial, being held in the U.S. District Court in Oxford, Miss. Henry Espy pleaded not guilty to charges laid against him.

Last December, Ferrouillet and John Hemmingson, the chairman of the country's second-largest crop insurance firm, were convicted of fraudulently obtaining and then laundering a $20,000 campaign contribution for Henry Espy.
Mike Espy stepped down as agriculture secretary in 1994 because of the allegations he accepted illegal gifts and favors from firms he was responsible for overseeing.
